findings.passage: Today, Legislative Republicans have shown that their number one priority is passing a constitutional amendment that could disenfranchise voters because their austerity agenda is unpopular. There’s a historic legacy of voter suppression in Wisconsin’s Black communities – this is yet another attempt to silence the voices of Black, Brown and Indigenous people in Wisconsin.
findings.note: Statement issued in his name when the Assembly passed AJR 1, the voter ID constitutional amendment. He says the amendment could keep people from voting and ties it to past voter suppression. Date is from the official press release list (legis.wisconsin.gov/assembly/10/madison/news-updates/press-releases/).

findings.passage: The man who killed my brother and nearly killed my brother’s girlfriend was convicted of multiple felonies and should not have had access to a firearm. If Wisconsin had implemented common sense gun laws and this office was established, my brother would likely be alive today.
findings.note: In a press release issued in his name on the governor's Office of Violence Prevention, he says his brother was shot by a man with felony convictions and says common sense gun laws would likely have prevented the death.
subjects: keeping guns from people with felony convictions

findings.passage: Through the Wisconsin Office of Violence Prevention, the state can begin to establish a path to addressing the root causes of violence in our communities from common sense gun safety to reducing the criminalization of addiction to critical mental health services.
findings.note: He names common sense gun safety as one of the root-cause areas the new state office can address, alongside addiction policy and mental health services.
A line under the safety and justice priorities on his campaign site. The page carries no date.
